sources.title: Miami Tribe of Oklahoma: About and tribal history
sources.note: Direct/indexed tribal account: myaamia self-name, Great Lakes homeland, 1795 treaty, 1846 removal to Kansas and late 1860s-1870s moves to Oklahoma. Inconsistent removed population figures on the page omitted. Explicitly avoids treating 1867 treaty as a single exact migration day.

sources.title: Miami Nation of Indians of Indiana: History and Culture
sources.note: Direct contemporary community account, descendants who remained, river-linked villages and present programs. Page’s mistaken early-twentieth-century date for western Miami move to Oklahoma not adopted; western tribal account supplies that chronology. Current federal-status distinction directly stated.

sources.title: Cameron Shriver, Myaamia Center: Corn in Historical Sources, 2025
sources.note: Direct community historian’s analysis, early eighteenth-century Detroit commandant description and nineteenth/twentieth-century farming evidence. Source quotations not reproduced; no claim all Ohio Valley corn fields were exclusively Miami.

sources.title: Jared Nally, Myaamia Center: Picking Up the Threads, 2023
sources.note: Direct practicing Myaamia weaver’s account, bark and herbaceous fibers, processing and spinning time. Present research/revitalization perspective explicitly retained.

sources.title: Megan Mooney, Myaamia Center: What Are Myaamia Games?, 2022
sources.note: Direct Winter Games and Summer Games sections, snowsnake, contemporary annual Seneca-Cayuga lacrosse and new adaptations. Does not backdate modern adapted games to precontact life.

sources.title: Myaamia Center: Maple Sugaring 2024
sources.note: Direct report of 2024 camps in Ohio, Indiana and Oklahoma. Approximately 40 gallons maple sap per gallon syrup as customary yield estimate, not a universal exact ratio; black walnut adaptation in Oklahoma.

sources.title: National Park Service: Chief Michikinikwa
sources.note: Direct military biography, coalition victories 1790 and 1791 and call for peace before 1794. Collective coalition role retained; no claim Miami alone defeated the United States.

sources.title: Myaamia Center Assessment Brief 4: Language Revitalization, 2019
sources.note: Direct two-page primary program report, page 1: archive-based language revitalization using documentation from late 1600s to 1960s. Page distinguishes gradual intergenerational work from a claim of universal fluency.

sources.title: Miami University, Miami Tribe Relations: Myaamia words with translations
sources.note: Direct FAQ section Myaamia Words With Translations: exact Tipeewe neeyolaani / It is good to see you. Modern institutional/community teaching spelling. Also documents Myaamia Project 2001 and Center 2013. Inconsistent degree/graduation counters not used.

sources.title: Myaamia Center: 2023 Summer Program Recap and Outcomes
sources.note: Direct primary program report: ages 10-16, miniature lodges simulating elm bark/cattail mats, documentary and family-tree language exercises. These are modern learning activities about older lifeways.

sources.title: Miami University Libraries: Daily Receipts by the Miami Canal, Myaamia Removal exhibition
sources.note: Original indexed university archival exhibit states five canal boats arrived Cincinnati October 11,1846 and forced transfer to Colorado. Direct fetch 502; original targeted search reproduced opening. Description of evidence does not assert visual inspection of receipt image. Reproducible query: site:migrations.lib.miamioh.edu/s/the-forced-removal-of-the-Myaamia/page/daily-receipts-by-the-miami-canal "October 11th" "five".

sources.title: Citizen Potawatomi Nation Cultural Heritage Center: History
sources.note: Direct chronology: French trade, 1838 Trail of Death, 1861 Citizen Potawatomi treaty and 1872 arrivals in Indian Territory. Does not generalize Citizen Potawatomi history to every Potawatomi nation or convert traditional migration chronology into a firmly dated archaeological event.

sources.title: Forest County Potawatomi: Timeline of Potawatomi History
sources.note: Direct Three Fires affiliation, Wisconsin/French trade and Forest County continuation. Differing origin chronologies across community accounts acknowledged; no exact split year imposed.

sources.title: Pokagon Band of Potawatomi: Our Culture and History
sources.note: Direct account of Leopold Pokagon, 1833 treaty exception, purchase near Dowagiac and continued community, federal reaffirmation 1994. Approximate Trail of Death figures on this page not adopted; CPN source used for that event.

sources.title: CPN Cultural Heritage Center: Pre-European Contact Lifeways, 2018
sources.note: Direct curator Blake Norton and seamstress Gayla Mosteller on seasonal living, shelters, diverse moon names and games. No literal universal inference from a modern museum reconstruction; no medical efficacy claims.

sources.title: Citizen Potawatomi Nation: Saving the Good Seed, 2019
sources.note: Direct community specialists describe canoe harvesting and reseeding, plus specific father’s account of two sons trying rice porridge. No broad nutritional superiority or speculative precise ancient settlement date adopted.

sources.title: CPN Cultural Heritage Center: Marine Exhibit, 2013
sources.note: Direct museum description of reconstructed birchbark-canoe spearfishing scene and tools; clearly a modern interpretation of older lifeways, not an ancient surviving canoe.

sources.title: National Museum of the American Indian: Prairie Band Potawatomi cradleboard
sources.note: Direct original catalogue 2/7492; made 1880-1900, Kansas Prairie Band, collected from Ci-pa-do-wa in 1910, carved wood/hide ties/glass beads/cotton. Date of production distinguished from collection.

sources.title: Justin Neely, CPN Language Department: Language with Justin, April 2016
sources.note: Direct bilingual self-introduction Bodéwadmi ndaw. / I am Potawatomi. Also explicitly equates Bodéwadmi and Potawatomi, distinguishing related Anishinaabe peoples; not a translation of full imported alias string.

sources.title: Justin Neely, CPN Language Department: Language Update, December 2022
sources.note: Direct first-person department report: children’s books,3500 translated words/audio for Woolaroo and camera-based object vocabulary. Historical 2022 project, no promise current third-party app still operates.

sources.title: Citizen Potawatomi Nation: Joining the Bodéwadmi Confederation,2026
sources.note: Direct dated report: July 2025 formation and CPNJuly 30,2026 signing, rotating administration, distinct member nations. Conflicting last-paragraph future gathering date and unstable exact membership count omitted.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Direct Miami Tribe self-identification says myaamia, pronounced Miami. Historical main footprint in Indiana and larger Myaamia Great Lakes footprint may share this people-level history, with public approximate-outline caveat. Preserve distinct modern Oklahoma Tribe and Indiana community identities; do not imply one modern government covers everyone. Miami-Oklahoma is accepted as a later location of the same people. Tribal history and university tribal-relations sources independently confirm the Oklahoma identity. Its 1492 map date is anachronistic; the public opening and removal section explicitly explain the nineteenth-century move. Shared association does not repair imported geometry or dates.

Michigan main outline and broader Great Lakes homeland outline refer to Potawatomi peoples; direct CPN self-name evidence confirms Bodéwadmi. Narrative explicitly distinguishes peoples from a centralized historical state and Citizen, Pokagon, Prairie Band and Forest County trajectories. No literal translation claimed for full imported alias. Exclude composite potawatomi-shawnee-oklahoma; Shawnee not absorbed.
